name: Staircase Subcube-Scaffold Contraction Obstructions
definition: Let $X=\{a,b,c,q\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}U$ with $U\ne\varnothing$. Delete the scaffold $\{\{a\},\{b\},\{a,b\},\{a,c\}\}$, every $\{a,b,c\}\cup T$ with $T\subseteq U$, and the optional states $\{b,c\}$, $\{b,q\}$, $\{c\}$, $\{a,b,q\}$ selected respectively by $\gamma,\beta,\eta,\lambda$. The base is the complement in $2^X$; attach a new pendant coordinate $f$ at the empty endpoint.
parameters: $d=|X|\ge5$, $U\ne\varnothing$, $\gamma,\beta,\eta,\lambda\in\{0,1\}$, $\gamma+\beta\le1$, $\eta\le\gamma$, and $\lambda\le\beta$. The pendant family has $2^d-2^{d-4}-3-\gamma-\beta-\eta-\lambda$ states.
canonical_form: The parameters select compatible decorations of a four-state staircase scaffold attached to the anchored subcube $\{\{a,b,c\}\cup T:T\subseteq U\}$.
recognition: A construction certificate checks the valid root $\{b,c\}$ when $\gamma=0$ and $\{a,b,c,q\}$ when $(\gamma,\beta)=(1,0)$, the exact endpoint hole sets, and repair sets $\{a,b,c,q\}$ and $U\cup\{q\}$ for $\beta=0$ or $U$ for $\beta=1$.
comments: Every member is contraction-minimal outside learning-space graphs. No pc-minimality or completeness claim is made because learning-space graphs are not closed under convex restrictions.
